case_info.explanation: Histological examination revealed trabecular bone without epithelial elements, and immunohistochemical staining for cytokeratin (AE1/AE3) was negative. The bone marrow demonstrated normal trilineage hematopoiesis, with no evidence of malignancy. Although positron emission tomography (PET)/CT was not performed at that time, a retrospective review of a PET/CT scan obtained 3 years earlier revealed mild fluorodeoxyglucose uptake in the thoracolumbar vertebral bodies (Figure 2). In the context of the patient’s clinical and imaging findings, these results are supportive of bone pseudometastasis.1This phenomenon has been predominantly reported in East Asian patients with esophageal cancer and, less frequently, in head and neck cancers.2,3 While biopsy remains the criterion standard for establishing the diagnosis, several imaging features can suggest bone pseudometastasis. Typical imaging shows hypointense lesions on T1/T2 MRI and mild hyperdensity without cortical destruction on CT.1Although these findings are nonspecific, the absence of aggressive features such as cortical destruction or soft tissue extension may help raise suspicion for a benign process. Serial imaging is also informative, as pseudometastatic lesions typically remain stable over time. In general, PET-CT may show mild fluorodeoxyglucose uptake with lower standardized uptake values but cannot reliably distinguish pseudometastasis from true metastasis.1,3 The pathophysiology of bone pseudometastasis remains incompletely understood. Proposed mechanisms include alterations of the marrow microenvironment associated with chronic alcohol consumption and ALDH2 deficiency, which may influence hematopoietic activity, a hypothesis supported by frequent reports in Japanese patients with esophageal cancer, where ALDH2 deficiency is a known risk factor. Prostate metastases are typically osteoblastic with T1 low and T2 iso-low signal plus restricted diffusion, usually in older men with high prostate-specific antigen, which was absent here.5Answer C was incorrect as well.
